about: Living Roots Wine & Co. was founded in 2016 by Sebastian and Colleen Hardy, and makes wine in two hemispheres. Seb comes from six generations of Australian winemakers: his great-great-great-grandfather Thomas Hardy arrived in South Australia in 1850 and planted some of its first vines. Colleen, a Rochester native who left marketing for the cellar, met him while working a vintage at Hardy’s Tintara winery. They make Finger Lakes wine at an urban winery in Rochester and red wines in the Adelaide Hills, and in 2023 Halliday’s Wine Companion named Living Roots Australia’s Best New Winery.

A pét-nat, short for pétillant naturel, is the oldest way of making sparkling wine. Rather than adding sugar and yeast for a second fermentation, the wine is bottled while its first fermentation is still going, and the last of the grape sugar finishes fermenting under the cap, trapping its carbon dioxide as a soft natural sparkle. For this wine the Hardys whole-bunch press Finger Lakes Riesling to keep bitterness low, ferment it with wild yeasts and finish it in bottle, completely dry, with no residual sugar.

On the Finger Lakes side the Hardys focus on cool-climate whites and sparkling wines, drawing on Colleen’s parents’ Shale Creek Vineyard above Keuka Lake, which takes part in New York’s Sustainable Winegrowing Program, and on fruit from growers around the region. Alongside this Riesling they have made pét-nats from Cayuga White and rosé. For this one they describe pithy lemon and juicy peach balanced by chalky minerality, fine natural bubbles and a bone-dry finish.
facts: Pétillant naturel: wild ferment finished in bottle
